rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 (study) is the rule's own named trigger example verbatim: 'cross-project ~/.claude/projects/ session scans.' Body callout coverage before the prompt (raw L22-28): L26 ('Cut the scan when the top patterns are clear enough to use... Narrow it whenever you like, or say tell me what you've found so far... you do not need a complete inventory') covers ONLY the over-reading/cut-it-short direction the rule names as (a). Nothing in the body — checked L17-28 in full — tells the student what to do if the scan comes back thin, stalls on one or two repos, or Claude declares a shallow pass done, which is failure direction (b) the rule requires naming explicitly ('nudge it to keep going, there's more here'). Harm: this prompt's own instruction is to look 'across everything I do' (L15) and the exercise body says 'Look wider than the two sessions... run across everything you do' (raw L19) — a premature stop directly undercuts the exercise's stated ask, and there's no recovery move on record for the student to use. Confirmed not a deliberate omission: the maintainer's own Failure-modes note (raw L109-110) names only the sprawl direction. Checked for an accept-note covering this gap — none found among the 6 dated notes in the maintainer/backing blocks (view.json accept_notes). The proactive counterpart, check_prompts.md §43 (progress-streaming), is satisfied (see below) and reduces but doesn't eliminate this: watching thin coverage stream by doesn't tell the student the specific recovery move is to say 'keep going' rather than accept the list.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add one clause to the existing raw-L26 callout (or immediately after it) naming the premature-stop direction with a paste-ready nudge in the same register, e.g. 'If the groups look thin, or keep coming from just one or two repos, tell it there's more here and let it keep going before you rank.'

Don't go quiet and hand me everything at the end.' rules_evaluated.evidence: Warm session, confirmed by reading the module body (per the rule's own method, not the frontmatter context: line): the exercise's session widget at raw L5 is '(continue, "Module 6 worktree session")' — same session, no /clear between producer and this prompt. §40b corollary (warm != referent-present): the definite-article reference 'the recurring groups you just named' (registry spot-gaps-build-the-loop-shapes.md L15) points at prompt 1 (study)'s own output, which ran as the immediately preceding turn in this same continued session — the referent is genuinely in scrollback, not a curriculum-coined label absent from the agent's context.

'Then evaluate fit for the dominant gap I named in Phase 1' (registry spot-gaps-build-the-loop-primitives.md L19) leans on a curriculum-coined label. Checked the sibling exercise curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md: 'Phase 1' appears only in maintainer-block prose (Failure-modes/Decision-points/Plug-points, lines 75/76/80/84/85/86) and 'a dominant gap' appears only in student-facing body prose (line 30) — neither string is typed into any prompt fence a student pastes (checked curriculum/prompts/spot-gaps-build-the-loop-1.md and -2.md in full: the ranking ask is 'which gap matters most? Rank by damage-to-a-future-session', never 'dominant gap' or 'Phase 1'). Per §40b's own tell ('definite article in front of a curriculum-coined noun phrase'), this is the pattern the rule names. Practical risk stays low, not high: this same continued session (per the exercise's own framing, 'Same session as the gap map... in scrollback') contains exactly one ranked-gap output to resolve against, so an LLM's pragmatic reference resolution is very likely to land correctly even without the literal string match — there's no second candidate for 'the gap' to be confused with.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rephrase to the in-scrollback action rather than the curriculum label, e.g. 'the gap you ranked highest a few prompts back' instead of 'the dominant gap I named in Phase 1'.
